preamble.title: The case - Loki
preamble.html: The case. Loki is a 14 year old boy who has had Type 1 diabetes for 8 years. He is currently receiving NPH at breakfast and at bedtime, and Novorapid at breakfast and suppertime. His insulin is injected into his legs and abdomen. He checks his blood glucose levels four times daily. He is seen regularly in a pediatric diabetes clinic and his most recent hemogloblin A1C is 8.4%.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 46-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes is maintained on insulin glargine 30 units daily, insulin lispro 10 units three times daily with meals, and glimepiride. Her fasting glucose has been running 5.5-7.0 mmol/L but her 2-hour post-prandial readings are consistently 15-18 mmol/L, and her A1C is 11.0%. Over the following 21 months her BMI falls from 45.6 to 17.0 (weight 42 kg) despite escalating insulin. She is cachectic with diffuse loss of fat and muscle, and has developed acromegaly-like facial features, extensive acanthosis nigricans, skin tags and vitiligo. Her A1C remains 11.0-14.0% and her total insulin requirement now exceeds 50 units/kg/day.

preamble.title: The case - Molly
preamble.html: The case. Molly Flanders is a 26-year-old woman with 5 cycles in the past year, acne and excess facial hair. She has had no period for 4 months, and in the last two months has been up at least once a night with nocturia and has had three yeast infections. She and her partner would like to have a baby. Exam: height 1.50 m, weight 81 kg (BMI ~36 kg/m²), BP 135/85, mild facial hirsutism, acanthosis and skin tags on the neck, no Cushingoid stigmata. Labs: A1c 6.7%, fasting plasma glucose 7.4 mmol/L.

preamble.title: The case - adrenal insufficiency, 19-year-old woman
preamble.html:
The case. A 19-year-old woman. PMH: hypothyroidism (well-controlled), infiltrative keratitis, mononucleosis, occasional headaches. Medications: levothyroxine 75 µg OD, ibuprofen 200 mg PRN, never steroids. FH: hypothyroidism (mother, aunt), type 1 diabetes (cousin).

Over 3-4 years: weight loss (dress size 7 to 0, non-intentionally), weakness, fatigability, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, orthostatic presyncope, and multiple infections.

Over the last 3 months: two infections resulting in hospitalisation, one progressing to a 5-day ICU stay for a urinary tract infection and acute kidney injury secondary to Group-B Streptococcus, with low blood pressure that was hard to treat. More recently an upper respiratory tract infection, at which point she was started on hydrocortisone.

preamble.title: The case - vertebral fracture, 41-year-old man
preamble.html: The case. In 2001, a then 41-year-old man, director of a smaller NGO, university educated, presented with back pain (thoracic spine). X-ray showed some vertebral collapse. There was no trauma. His lumbar T-score is -2.6. He reports easy fatiguability and low sex drive, with no heat or cold intolerance, and shaves daily. His testosterone measures 5 and 7.8 nmol/L against a normal range of 10.5-34.5.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. You are asked to see a 7 yr old girl for growth assessment.Her height is 110 cm ( 1st percentile) and weight is 25 kg ( 75th percentile). Mother measures 160 cm and father measures 180 cm. In further assessment, you notice that her height was 109 cm (10th percentile) one year ago at age 5.5 yrs. She had a normal birth weight and length. Mother reported a normal pregnancy with no complications. She had "low sugar" in the neonatal period but resolved in 48-72 hrs. CBC, ferritin, renal function were normal.

preamble.title: The case - Marnie
preamble.html: The case. Over the phone, your friend Marnie tells you that she is sad because her manicurist made mean comments about her nails. Some insults include: “Your nails have pits and ridges, yellow dots and dark streaks, and are basically lifting right off. Your fingers also look like sausages.” Your friend is also stressed because she thinks she has relentless dandruff, pinkeye, and arthritis in her knees. You suspect your friend actually has a type of spondyloarthritis.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 60-year-old male with a large left-sided ischemic stroke sustains significant right-sided paresis of his arm. When asked what has happened to his right arm, he states nothing it's fine.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 70-year-old RHD male develops acute onset left arm weakness and numbness. Within 24hrs he then goes on to start speaking nonsense that no one appears to understand. In the hospital you note that he has only shaved the right side of his face and has not put his arm through his left sleeve. On neurological examination he is unable to repeat phrases and follow three step commands however his fluency is unaffected. You are unable to check his strength and sensation as he cannot understand instructions but he is found to be hyperreflexic in his left arm.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 65-year-old woman presents to your clinic complaining of episodic vertigo over the past three weeks. Her initial episode occurred when she was lying down in bed and rolled over from her right to left side. She stated that the vertigo woke her up and felt like the "room was spinning." The episodes only last for seconds and are aggravated by very specific head movements, such as when looking up to reach for something from her cupboard. She claims the vertigo is associated with nausea but no vomiting.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 40-year-old woman is admitted to the emergency department after her family found her in a confused state at her home. Upon initial evaluation, she is found to be disoriented and lethargic. CN nerve exam revealed horizontal nystagmus and diplopia but was otherwise normal. On motor and sensory exam reflexes, power, and sensation was normal throughout. She did exhibit bilateral dysmetria with finger to nose and heel to shin testing and had a severely ataxic gait. On history it is found that the patient has undergone roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery, there is no history of head trauma.

preamble.title: The case - Tom Paris
preamble.html: The case. Tom Paris presents with complaints of foot drop and difficulty swallowing. On history it is discovered that the weakness has been progressively getting worse over a number of months, and on physical examination you discover signs of atrophy, fasciculations, hyperreflexia, and spasticity. There is no evidence of sensory, bladder, or coordination issues. These findings are consistent in both the cervical and the lumbosacral regions. You order an MRI and are able to rule out any structural causes for these symptoms.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 36-year-old male presents to your family practice with a concern of dizziness. He says the episodes last for about 30 seconds, are typically triggered when he “moves too fast,” and when they occur it feels like the room is “spinning around him.” He denies any changes in hearing. He does not take any medications and his past medical history is unremarkable.

preamble.title: The case - Beverly
preamble.html: The case. Beverly is a 24-year-old woman followed by you for major depression. You have decided that the best treatment option for her is an SSRI. Beverly tells you that she often forgets to take medications on time.

preamble.title: The case - Maria
preamble.html: The case. When you go to see Maria for your initial assessment, she is wearing a black cocktail dress and large silver earrings. She agrees quite happily to answer your questions, and tells you that she was picked up by the police because she was outside in the middle of December wearing only this dress. When you ask her if she feels that this was safe, she tells you that "my love will keep me warm". Upon further questioning, she reveals that she was walking to a hotel where she believes that George Clooney is waiting to spend a romantic evening with her. She describes herself as feeling extremely happy and energetic, but does not believe that there is anything unusual happening. She denies any suicidal or homicidal ideation.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 32-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a history of taking two different medications: sertraline for depression and tramadol for chronic pain. The patient reports feeling agitated, confused, and experiencing tremors and muscle stiffness. He also complains of sweating and a rapid heart rate.

preamble.title: The case - Anais
preamble.html: The case. Anais is a ten-year-old girl who you have diagnosed with clinical depression. Her mother also has clinical depression and tells you that she is confused by your diagnosis, since Anais' mood does not at all resemble what the mother experiences when she is depressed.

preamble.title: The case - Brenda
preamble.html: The case. Brenda is a 19-year-old woman who is currently undergoing treatment for breast cancer, and presents to you with concerns about her mood. Her appetite is decreased, she has no desire to see her friends, and she cries for most of the day. She does not sleep well and complains of initial insomnia as well as frequent awakenings. You wonder if you should prescribe an SSRI to help with her symptoms.

preamble.title: The case - Meg
preamble.html: The case. Meg is a 25-year-old woman who comes to your office complaining about persistent anxiety. She tells you that she constantly worries about the future and thinks about everything that could possibly go wrong with her job, her health, and her finances. She often needs to call her husband during the day to "check" that he is still alive.

preamble.title: The case - Mallory
preamble.html: The case. Mallory is a young woman who presents to your office complaining of sudden shortness of breath, chest pain, and a choking sensation in her throat. When this occurs, she feels scared that she is having a heart attack and will often go to the emergency department. Despite multiple tests, she feels sure that she has a heart condition and is no longer willing to leave her house because of concerns that she will have an attack and not be able to get help.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 27-year-old female is presenting with recurrent and persistent episodes of excessive worry and fear about a variety of things, along with restlessness, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, muscle tension, and sleep disturbance.

preamble.title: The case - Pierre
preamble.html: The case. Pierre is a 47-year-old male who lives with his wife and son. His wife brings him to your office complaining that he is "making her miserable". He refuses to allow anyone else to do household tasks, such as washing dishes, because they "don't do it right". If someone does wash a dish, Pierre must wash it again to make sure it is really clean. He has few friends and frequently volunteers to work long hours at his job so that he can save more money, rather than spend time with his family. When you ask Pierre about this, he says that he does not have a problem and that really it is everyone else who doesn't know how to do things the right way.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 10-year-old boy presents to the clinic with a history of struggling in school. He has difficulty with reading and writing, often misspelling words and having difficulty with sentence structure. He also struggles with math concepts and has difficulty with basic calculations. He has had difficulty keeping up with his peers academically and has been receiving tutoring for several months. His teacher reports that he is easily distracted and has difficulty following instructions. He has no significant medical history.

preamble.title: The case - Andy
preamble.html: The case. Andy is a 12-year-old boy who has been brought to you for an evaluation because he has been refusing to attend school.

preamble.title: The case
preamble.html: The case. A 17-year-old female presents to the clinic with a concern for weight loss. She has lost approximately 20 pounds over the past three months, and reports restricting her caloric intake to less than 800 calories per day. She reports feeling guilty or ashamed after eating, and denies any episodes of binge eating or purging. She reports an intense fear of gaining weight, and reports feeling fat despite being underweight. She reports missing her menstrual period for the past three months. She denies any significant medical history.

preamble.title: The case - Jerry
preamble.html: The case. Jerry is an 85-year-old male who is brought to your office by his wife, who has noticed that he is experiencing increased difficulty with his memory and cognition. She also notes that he no longer enjoys his hobbies the way that he used to.

preamble.title: The case - Alexa
preamble.html: The case. Alexa is a 40 year old female with bleeding between periods and daily spotting. Her cycles are 27 days with 7 days of bleeding, she is on no medications and has no other bleeding. Her BP is 122/80, HR 75, RR 15, temp 37.5. Her exam is normal except for a small fleshy 2 cm cervical mass.

preamble.title: The case - Alice
preamble.html: The case. Alice is a 29 year old female with the clinical diagnosis of Neurofibromatosis type 1. She had a molecular test that confirmed an NF1 pathogenic mutation. She is aware that it is a dominant condition with a 50% chance of recurrence. She is now pregnant and is interested in prenatal diagnosis.
